latest_release.name: 2026.47.8 (alpha)
latest_release.body:
Ladybird 2026.47.8 restores sound on macOS and fixes several crashes. It also fixes DNS lookups on Linux after the network reconnects, and a Gmail search box that collapsed.

Ladybird updates itself on macOS and through the package manager on Linux, or you can download it from https://ladybird.org/download/.

## Web compatibility

- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15775: Gmail no longer collapses its search box until the window is resized. Scripts inserted together with a subtree now read correct element sizes.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15429: A 2D `<canvas>` larger than the GPU's maximum texture size no longer crashes the compositor. It is now drawn from memory instead of staying blank.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15126: Fixed a crash when reading `offsetParent`, and empty `getComputedStyle()` results. Both happened with slotted elements that moved between hidden and shown slots, and one crash was reported on a YouTube watch page.

## Media

- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15555: Fixed an issue that could leave Ladybird with no audio output on macOS.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15605: Fixed a video decoder process crash when an AV1 video switched to a larger size, for example when changing quality on YouTube.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15605, https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15744: Prevented broken video playback when a media or video decoder process is exiting while a new video is starting to load.

## Networking

- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/14605: On Linux, pages no longer fail with "Unable to resolve host" after NetworkManager replaces `/etc/resolv.conf`, for example when you reconnect to a network.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/14605: A proxy given by host name is now resolved the same way as other hosts.

## Stability

- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15663: Fixed crashes when a click moved focus and the focus styles also cancelled an animation and changed scroll snapping. The same fix may also help with crashes while the accessibility tree is built.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15695: Fixed a macOS crash when assistive technology asked about a tab that had been closed.

## Platforms

- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15765: On Linux machines without an NVIDIA GPU, the NVIDIA driver no longer causes a crash.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15418: Fixed a crash when creating a WebGL context on Linux builds made with older headers, such as Ubuntu 24.04.
- https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/pull/15458: Wayland fixes for the Qt interface. Builds made with Qt 6.10 now work with the Qt 6.11 runtime, and a crash when moving a tab between windows is fixed.

detail.readme:
# Ladybird

[Ladybird](https://ladybird.org) is a truly independent web browser, using a novel engine based on web standards.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Ladybird is in a pre-alpha state, and only suitable for use by developers
>

## Features

We aim to build a complete, usable browser for the modern web.

Ladybird uses a [multi-process architecture](Documentation/ProcessArchitecture.md) with a main UI process,
WebContent renderer processes, and helper processes for tasks such as networking, image decoding, compositing and media.

Documents from different sites run in separate renderer processes, each sandboxed from the rest of the system.
Image decoding and network connections are done out of process, separately for each site, to be more robust against
malicious content.

At the moment, many core library support components are inherited from SerenityOS:

- LibWeb: Web rendering engine
- LibJS: JavaScript engine
- LibWasm: WebAssembly implementation
- LibCrypto/LibTLS: Cryptography primitives and Transport Layer Security
- LibHTTP: HTTP/1.1 client
- LibGfx: 2D Graphics Library, Image Decoding and Rendering
- LibUnicode: Unicode and locale support
- LibMedia: Audio and video playback
- LibCore: Event loop, OS abstraction layer
- LibIPC: Inter-process communication

## How do I build and run this?

See [build instructions](Documentation/BuildInstructionsLadybird.md) for information on how to build Ladybird.

Ladybird runs on Linux, macOS, Windows (with WSL2), and many other \*Nixes.

## How do I read the documentation?

Code-related documentation can be found in the [documentation](Documentation/) folder.

## Get in touch and participate!

Join [our Discord server](https://discord.gg/nvfjVJ4Svh) to participate in issue and development discussions.

Please read [Getting involved with Ladybird](Documentation/GettingStartedContributing.md) if you're new to Ladybird and want to help.

Before opening an issue, please see the [issue policy](CONTRIBUTING.md#issue-policy) and the [detailed issue-reporting guidelines](ISSUES.md).

The project participation guidelines can be found in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md).
